newsitem.title: TAIWAN: GTE to join Pacific mobile plan.
newsitem.headline: GTE to join Pacific mobile plan.

text.p: The U.S.-based GTE Corp Corp said on Friday it would join a T$6 billion telecommunication venture led by Taiwan's Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd to do mobile telephone businesses on the island.
"After careful evaluation, GTE... has decided to join Pacific's project to seek mobile phone licence in the Taiwan region," GTE said in a statement.
GTE did not say how much stake it would own in the venture.
The statement said that Taiwan's Yageo Corp, Evergreen Marine Corp and Acer Inc were among the other investors in the deal.
Pacific had said it would take up 10 percent of the deal, but declined to reveal the stakes of other participating members.
GTE would offer technological assistance to Pacific Wire under the terms of the venture, GTE's statement said without elaborating.
Mobile telephony is one of several telecom sectors liberalised by Taiwan's parliament in January 1996, opening them up for private and foreign investments.
Before the reforms, telephone, data and other telecom services had been monopolised by the Directorate General of Telecommunications.
The liberalisation surged ahead on July 1 as the monopoly's operations were spun off as Chunghwa Telecommunications Corp.
